title: Cases Review: Nom, Acc, Gen
intro: Let's review the first three Russian cases! Nominative (Кто? Что?) is used for the subject — the person or thing doing the action. Accusative (Кого? Что?) marks the direct object — what the action is done to, and also direction (в школу). Genitive (Кого? Чего?) shows possession (книга брата), absence (нет воды), and is used after numbers and certain prepositions (из, от, без, у). Knowing which case to use depends on the word's role in the sentence.
rules: Nominative (Им.): The subject of the sentence — who or what does the action. Кто? Что? — Мама читает. Студент работает.
Accusative (Вин.): The direct object — what receives the action, and direction. Кого? Что? Куда? — Читаю книгу. Иду в школу. Animate masculine nouns look like genitive: вижу брата.
Genitive (Род.): Possession, absence, 'of', after numbers 2-4, and genitive prepositions. Кого? Чего? — Книга друга. Нет молока. Два стула. Из магазина.
Key test: Nominative = who is doing? Accusative = what is affected? Genitive = whose, or what is absent/counted?
examples: Студент читает книгу. — The student (nom.) reads a book (acc.).
Это машина брата. — This is the brother's (gen.) car (nom.).
Нет молока. — There is no milk (gen.).
Я вижу маму. — I see mom (acc.).
У друга есть собака. — A friend (gen.) has a dog (nom.).

items.prompt: _____ работает в магазине. (The brother works in the store.)
items.promptEnglish: The brother works in the store.
items.hint: Who is doing the action? Subject = nominative
items.explanation: The subject of the sentence uses nominative case: Брат.

items.hint: What am I buying? Direct object, inanimate masculine
items.explanation: Хлеб is inanimate masculine, so accusative = nominative: хлеб.

items.prompt: Это машина _____. (This is the father's car.)
У меня нет _____. (I don't have a pen.)
items.explanation: Нет (don't have / there is no) takes genitive: ручка → ручки.
Кошка is feminine, so accusative: кошка → кошку.

items.prompt: _____ лежит на столе. (The book is lying on the table.)
items.promptEnglish: The book is lying on the table.
items.hint: What is lying on the table? Subject
items.explanation: The subject of the sentence uses nominative: Книга.

items.prompt: Я иду в _____. (I'm going to the store.)
items.explanation: Direction uses в + accusative. Магазин is inanimate masculine, so accusative = nominative: магазин.

items.prompt: Два _____ стоят на полке. (Two cups are standing on the shelf.)
items.promptEnglish: Two cups are standing on the shelf.
items.explanation: After два/две the noun takes genitive singular: стакан → стакана.

items.prompt: Мы знаем этого _____. (We know this student.)
items.hint: Direct object, animate masculine = genitive form
items.explanation: Студент is animate masculine. Accusative = genitive form: студента.

blanks: Я пришёл из _____. (I came from the store.)
hints: The preposition из (from) always takes genitive case. What is the genitive of магазин?
explanations: Из (from) requires genitive case. Masculine nouns ending in a consonant add -а: магазин → магазина.

minimalPairs.explanation: Direct object uses accusative: книга → книгу. Genitive книги would mean 'of the book' or 'no book'.

minimalPairs.context: У меня нет _____. (I don't have a book.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Нет (absence) takes genitive: книга → книги. Accusative книгу would be for a direct object.

explanations: Feminine -а nouns change to -у in accusative: мама → маму
Feminine -а nouns change to -ы in genitive: мама → мамы

Кого? Чего? — Нет молока. Книга друга.
